official_competition_sources.title: DrivenData DOE GEMS Prize Challenge Overview
official_competition_sources.authority: U.S. Department of Energy Geothermal Technologies Office / DrivenData
official_competition_sources.verified_facts: Two-phase $300,000 challenge ($50k Phase 1 top-5 split; $250k Phase 2 re-scoring the single final submission on expert-expanded labels); 100 m EPSG:32611 grid; Distance-Weighted Tversky Index (alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300 m linear decay).

official_competition_sources.title: DrivenData DOE GEMS Public Leaderboard
official_competition_sources.verified_facts: Historical snapshot only. Public leaderboard #1 was 0.4544 when reviewed on 2026-10-27; see docs/data/leaderboard.json and the source URL for updates.

official_competition_sources.title: Official GEMS Prize Reference Solution (Prof. John Lipor, Portland State University)
official_competition_sources.verified_facts: Confirms 19-band training_features.tif order, single-band float32 GTiff output in [0, 1] matching sample_submission.tif grid (3730x3292, EPSG:32611), and Tversky alpha=0.2, beta=0.8.

official_geoscience_data_sources.title: USGS GeoDAWN Airborne Geophysical & Radiometric Survey (NV/CA)
official_geoscience_data_sources.verified_facts: Provides airborne magnetic (TMI, TMI_up150) and gamma-ray spectrometry (K, eTh, eU, TC, Th/K, U/K, U/Th) grids across the GeoDAWN Basin-and-Range footprint.

official_geoscience_data_sources.title: Great Basin Center for Geothermal Energy INGENIOUS Regional Dataset (GDR #1391)
official_geoscience_data_sources.authority: DOE Geothermal Data Repository / UNR Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology
official_geoscience_data_sources.verified_facts: Provides regional thermal wells/springs with quartz/chalcedony/Na-K-Ca geothermometers, 2 m shallow temperature probes (F2mDAB above-background residual), volcanic vents, and Quaternary fault attributes.

official_geoscience_data_sources.title: INGENIOUS Paleo-Geothermal Surface Manifestations (Siliceous Sinter, Travertine, Tufa, Hydrothermal Breccia)
official_geoscience_data_sources.verified_facts: Distinguishes high-temperature siliceous sinter (>180 C deep reservoir indicator) and hydrothermal explosion breccia from lacustrine shoreline tufa mounds (Lake Lahontan non-geothermal mimic).

official_geoscience_data_sources.title: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) 1 m LiDAR Scarp Derivatives
official_geoscience_data_sources.verified_facts: Provides 1 m LiDAR scarp step height, crest/toe curvature dipole, facing asymmetry, 100 m strike coherence, and strike azimuth over 75.40% of the GEMS footprint (leaving a 24.60% LiDAR-void swath).

official_geoscience_data_sources.title: USGS State Geologic Map Compilation (SGMC) Fault Traces
official_geoscience_data_sources.verified_facts: Used strictly as an external off-catalogue validation benchmark (GEMSDOE32-SGMC-CAL-v3.0, 62,703 off-catalogue pixels); strictly excluded from HTCADS feature construction and model fitting.

official_geoscience_data_sources.title: USGS ScienceBase Great Basin Heat Flow Points
official_geoscience_data_sources.verified_facts: Borehole heat-flow measurements (mW/m^2) across the Great Basin.

peer_reviewed_literature.citation: Faulds, J. E., Coolbaugh, M. F., Blewitt, G., & Henry, C. D. (2004); Faulds, J. E., & Hinz, N. H. (2015). Favorable tectonic and structural settings of geothermal systems in the Great Basin region, western USA: Proxies for discovering blind geothermal systems. Proceedings World Geothermal Congress 2015.
peer_reviewed_literature.relevance: Establishes that ~39% of Great Basin geothermal systems are blind (no surface hot springs) and >75% localize in fault terminations (horsetail splays), dilational step-overs/relay ramps, and fault intersections rather than planar mid-segment range-front fault cores.

peer_reviewed_literature.citation: Grauch, V. J. S., & Hudson, M. R. (2007). Guides to understanding the aeromagnetic expression of faults in sedimentary basins: Lessons learned from the central Rio Grande rift, New Mexico. Geosphere, 3(6), 596-623; Blakely, R. J. (1995). Potential Theory in Gravity and Magnetic Applications.
peer_reviewed_literature.relevance: Proves that over dipping Basin-and-Range normal faults (dip 50-60 deg), the maximum horizontal gravity gradient (HGM) crest migrates basinward (downdip into the hanging wall) with source depth, whereas upward continuation tracks dip direction and enables updip surface-trace back-projection.

peer_reviewed_literature.citation: Gallardo, L. A., & Meju, M. A. (2004). Joint two-dimensional DC resistivity and seismic travel time inversion with cross-gradients constraints. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth, 109(B3).
peer_reviewed_literature.relevance: Defines the structural cross-gradient tensor coupling independent physical fields whose co-aligned gradients suppress single-modality lithologic mimics.

peer_reviewed_literature.citation: Coolbaugh, M. F., Sladek, C., Faulds, J. E., Zehner, R. E., & Oppliger, G. L. (2007); Kratt, C., Coolbaugh, M., Peppin, B., & Sladek, C. (2010). Shallow 2 m temperature surveys for blind geothermal discovery in the Great Basin. Geothermal Resources Council Transactions.
peer_reviewed_literature.relevance: Demonstrates that shallow 2 m thermal outflow plumes migrate laterally down the hydraulic gradient in basin-fill alluvium from their feeder range-front/piedmont fault conduit.

peer_reviewed_literature.citation: Dinkelbach, W. (1967). On nonlinear fractional programming. Management Science, 13(7), 492-498; Minoux, M. (1978). Accelerated greedy algorithms for maximizing submodular set functions.
peer_reviewed_literature.relevance: Proves exact fractional-linear optimality of binary {0, 1} allocation under expected Distance-Weighted Tversky Index and lazy-greedy CELF submodular cover.
